product.schneider-euro486-20-90.summary: The higher capacity option in the 1991 announcement.
product.schneider-euro486-20-90.history: In September 1991, the Euro486 offer with an 89 MB disk cost about DM 4,700. Schneider introduced it for desktop publishing, graphics and network workstations. The manual lists an HD 90 and the 1992 Portuguese advertisement names it /20–90.
product.schneider-euro486-20-90.technica: The sources give two disk figures. Computerwoche specifies 89 MB and the manual lists 90 MB, part 54 042 00. The drive installed in a specimen still needs identification.

The board integrates memory and video. Schneider signs the Singleboard 486 schematic for board 53 854 00 in the HD 40 and HD 90. The parts list identifies VLSI VL82C330/331/332, BIGJIM and ATI 28800-5.
One EPROM combines boot and video firmware. For board 53 854 00, the schematic places system and VGA in U16, a 128 KiB 27C010, part 53 891 00. An attributed dump remains to be preserved.
The configuration is documented. A dedicated model and boot in BluMach remain pending.
Attributed firmware, validation of the board map and an image with clear publication rights are still needed.
